bare_s1.explanation: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles, especially cars, pickups and vans, and fires most strongly on red or reddish-brown car bodies. It responds more weakly to related things such as red boats, kayaks, buses, fire and rescue vehicles, and a few red-accented non-vehicle scenes.

parsed.explanation: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles, especially cars, pickups and vans, and fires most strongly on red or reddish-brown car bodies. It responds more weakly to related things such as red boats, kayaks, buses, fire and rescue vehicles, and a few red-accented non-vehicle scenes.
parsed.evidence: 15 of the top 20 are road vehicles (convertibles, pickups, wagons, an ambulance, an FDNY truck, a bus), and many are red. The lower-ranked hits are red boats or kayaks, a red stretcher, a tent scene and a table, while the random photos with no vehicle or red object stay at 1-3.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on cars of controlled colors (for example non-red cars versus red non-vehicle objects) would show whether the unit encodes vehicle shape or red-colored objects.

Q0_s1.explanation: The unit responds mainly to motor vehicles, especially the body and window area of cars and pickups. It responds more weakly to other vehicles and conveyances such as boats, kayaks and a rescue stretcher, often when they are red.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds mainly to motor vehicles, especially the body and window area of cars and pickups. It responds more weakly to other vehicles and conveyances such as boats, kayaks and a rescue stretcher, often when they are red.
parsed.evidence: Ranks 1-15 are nearly all road vehicles (convertibles, pickups, a station wagon, a bus, an ambulance, a fire truck), and red is common among them. The lower-ranked hits are a red gondola-style boat, a kayak, a stretcher, plus a few outliers (tents, a table), while random photos score 1-3.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on red non-vehicle objects and on vehicles of other colors would show whether color or vehicle shape drives the response.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds to smooth, glossy, painted surfaces with long curved contours, crisp panel-like seams and bright specular highlights, most strongly when the color is a saturated red or orange-red. It also responds more weakly to the same glossy, shaped-panel look in white, silver or teal.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to smooth, glossy, painted surfaces with long curved contours, crisp panel-like seams and bright specular highlights, most strongly when the color is a saturated red or orange-red. It also responds more weakly to the same glossy, shaped-panel look in white, silver or teal.
parsed.evidence: Most of the top 20 show large, uniformly colored, reflective, smoothly curved panels with sharp edge lines, and red is common among them (#1, #4, #6-#10, #14, #15, #17). Lower-ranked hits are non-red glossy panels (#2, #3, #11, #20) or red/shiny shaped surfaces (#16, #19, #18), while the random images, which mostly show matte, textured or organic surfaces, stay at 1-3.
parsed.missing_data: Controlled images that separate glossiness and curved panel geometry from red color, such as red matte textured surfaces versus non-red glossy panels, would show which cue drives the unit.
